# Rift Gun 0.2.2-r2 for Minecraft 1.21.1

Rift Gun 0.2.2-r2 is a compatibility update for Xaero's Minimap 26.5.x.
It removes the startup rejection caused by Rift Gun's previous version ceiling.
Portal behavior, saved data, and configuration defaults are unchanged from r1.

## Highlights

- Allow Xaero's Minimap 26.5.x on both supported Minecraft versions.

# Rift Gun 0.2.2-r1 for Minecraft 1.21.1

Rift Gun 0.2.2-r1 adds per-gun appearance customization, independent Coordinate
and Pairing portal groups, and more flexible surface sizing and portal exits.
It also adds the Magic Circle visual, new sounds and shot animations, and fixes
portal rendering, remote facing, and reusable relocation targets.

Back up worlds before upgrading. Network protocol advances from 2 to 3;
player destination data remains at schema 11.

## Highlights

- Added Aperture-ish and Arcane Staff skins, with a Skin Module to unlock changes.
- Save portal visuals, sounds, and shot animation choices on each gun.
- Added a Color Module with HEX input and a color picker for display-only RGB.
- Added Magic Circle, Arcane sounds, Stars shot sound, and selectable shot animations.
- Keep Coordinate Travel and Portal Pairing portals open independently per player.
- Added a close-key radial for closing the portals of one mode.
- Added Full Support, Adaptive, and Prefer Large surface-size policies.
- Relaxed vertical exit collision checks and allowed floating portals below the world.

## Gun Appearance and Sound

- Added Aperture-ish and Arcane Staff, with dynamic fuel/mode
  colors and support for resource-pack skins. The new **Skin Module** unlocks
  changing the gun skin. Removing it keeps the selected skin.
- Skin, portal visual, shot animation, and sound choices
  are saved on each gun. Open portals keep the presentation captured when opened.
- Apply the current skin's recommended sounds, portal visual,
  and shot animation with one button. Three separate switches control automatic
  recommendations when applying a skin. Presets are editable in client config;
  `CUSTOM` keeps the gun's current choice.
- The Color Module customizes the gun and newly opened portals with a display-only
  RGB color. Choose with a hue wheel and saturation/value square, enter `#RRGGBB`,
  or restore the fuel color. Removing the module disables the override while
  preserving its setting. Fuel identity, consumption, cross-dimensional access,
  and instability are unaffected.
- Magic Circle is a new portal visual with glowing runes, triangles, and two
  inner rings, with separate inner/outer rotation controls.
- Added Arcane shot, portal, and transit sounds, plus a separate Stars
  shot sound. Increased Arcane shot loudness. Fresh Arcane Staff presets use
  Arcane sounds, Magic Circle, and Swing; existing saved presets are preserved.
- Choose Off, Light recoil, Swing, or Dip. Recoil strength
  and timing remain configurable on the client.

![newskin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/H3lic0pter/riftgun-assets/refs/heads/master/pics/newskin.png)

## Independent Coordinate and Pairing Portals

Each player can keep a Coordinate Travel portal pair and a Portal Pairing pair
at the same time. Opening or replacing one mode's portals leaves the other
mode's portals intact. Ownership is per player, not per gun.

- A short press of the close-portals key closes all of your portals.
- With Pairing available, hold that key to open a radial selector and close only
  Coordinate Travel or only Portal Pairing portals.
- The GUI close action continues to close all of your portals.

## Surface Portal Sizes

The **Portal Aperture Module** now offers three surface-size policies:

| Policy | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Full Support | Uses 2x2 only when the supporting surface is complete. |
| Adaptive (default) | Uses 1x2 on exposed vertical two-block support and 1x1 on the top/bottom of an isolated block; otherwise prefers 2x2 with overhang. |
| Prefer Large | Prefers 2x2 even when the supporting surface is incomplete. |

All three policies retain obstruction fallback. Adaptive and Prefer Large also
use the existing player-relative priority when choosing the portal's position.

- Ordinary vertical exits allow a closer exit position: approximately **0.41

# Rift Gun 0.2.1-r1 for Minecraft 26.1.2

Rift Gun 0.2.1-r1 turns Dimensional Navigation's Automatic Search into a
saved, reusable destination workflow. It also hardens queued-request lifecycle
checks, reduces destination snapshot size, and fixes paired-portal cleanup and
first-contact diagnostics.

Back up worlds before upgrading. This release advances player destination data
from schema 10 to schema 11.

## Highlights

- Automatic Search now saves a target in the virtual **Random** section instead
  of opening a portal immediately.
- Saved Automatic targets begin their bounded safe-location search only when
  used and can be reused for later portal opens.
- Pending searches are cancelled when their target changes, is deleted, or the
  owning player disconnects.
- Queued opens recheck policy, gun state, target identity, and fuel before
  continuing.
- Closed paired portals now remove both members of the pair.
- The first blocked-route diagnostic is shown immediately; later messages keep
  the existing 20-tick rate limit.

## Saved Automatic Search Targets

Dimensional Navigation's Automatic Search mode now follows the same save-first
workflow as exact-coordinate destinations.

- Saving creates an entry in the virtual **Random** section.
- Opening the entry starts the existing bounded random-rift search in the saved
  target dimension.
- The target can be pinned or deleted.
- Random-section expansion state is persisted with the player's destination
  data.
- Automatic targets cannot be renamed, moved into ordinary groups, or shared.
- Deleting or replacing a target cancels its pending search and releases its
  chunk tickets.
- Disconnecting the owning player also cancels pending work and releases
  tickets.
- Policy, gun state, target identity, and fuel are checked again before deferred
  preparation and before the final portal open.

The search itself retains the existing cooldown, world-border, placement,
chunk-readiness, fuel, and server-authority rules from 0.2.0-rc.1.

## Destination Data and Networking

- Player destination data advances from schema 10 to schema 11 for saved
  Automatic Search target state.
- Existing exact-coordinate destinations retain their dimension, coordinates,
  yaw, group, pin state, and display name.
- The destination model preserves text-target identity without copying source
  text into routine client snapshots.
- Missing text and intentionally empty text remain distinguishable in the client
  destination model.
- Shared text-data safeguards allow existing saves to load without truncation.

The network protocol remains `2`, but mixed 0.2.0-rc.1 and 0.2.1-r1
client/server installations are unsupported. Install the exact same Rift Gun
build on every peer.

## Portal Lifecycle and Diagnostics

- Closing either member of a paired portal now cleans up the linked member as
  well, preventing a stale partner entity from remaining in the world.
- The blocked-route notification cooldown now handles its uninitialized state
  explicitly. The first contact reports immediately instead of being suppressed
  by signed tick arithmetic overflow.
- Subsequent blocked-route diagnostics remain limited to once every 20 ticks.

## Stability and Performance

- Preserve first-in request order while advancing queued searches.
- Cancel absent-player searches and release their chunk tickets.
- Revalidate policy and fuel after queueing so changed conditions cannot open or
  charge a stale request.
- Bound deferred preparation waits to 200 ticks.
- Avoid copying persisted text source data into routine client snapshots.
- Added lifecycle, persistence, cancellation, timeout, policy, fuel, and
  platform-stub regression tests.
- Keep Infinite Dimensions preparation explicitly unavailable on this platform
  instead of attempting unsupported generation.
